ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering (as amended by Laws No. 181 of 2008 and No. 36 of 2014); Executive Regulations issued by the Central Bank of Egypt; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended); GAFI beneficial ownership disclosure regulations; Law No. 94 of 2015 on Combating Terrorism (financing and sanctions provisions); and ancillary Prime Ministerial decrees regulating the Commercial Registry UBO forms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy or national ID of each shareholder, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registration or passport authority of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issuer is in an Apostille Contracting State, otherwise Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing (for any corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution authorizing the Egyptian LLC incorporation and appointment of local representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or public notary of the foreign parent company

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney to the local incorporation attorney/agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the document's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Egypt's domestic terrorism and money laundering watchlist maintained by the Anti-Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Unit (AMLFU). Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for all Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates, with onboarding approval at senior management level. Continuous transaction and ownership-structure monitoring applies throughout the corporate lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Services Platform / Commercial Registry (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) – www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be transliterated into Arabic for registration with the Egyptian Commercial Registry; Latin-script names may be used in commercial correspondence but the official registered name is Arabic. The name must not be identical to an existing registered entity or trade name, must not include misleading or foreign titles, and must be followed by the appropriate company form indicator, e.g., LLC or S.A.E.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Commercial Registry Grievance Committee within 30 calendar days of the refusal, setting out the full grounds of law and fact; attach the original rejection note and have the local incorporation attorney prosecute the appeal. If the administrative appeal is denied, institute judicial recourse before the Administrative Economic Court within 60 days of the final GAFI decision. A fresh name reservation may be filed concurrently without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office not accepted for a commercial shipyard; the LLC must lease or own a physical office and operational shipyard/workshop in Egypt. The Egyptian Maritime Transport Sector and Industrial Development Authority require an on-site technical manager, registered land/berth, and safe access for maritime construction; a virtual office or postbox fails the substance and license conditions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 90% probability of unannounced inspection within the first year; maritime, tax, AML, and labour authorities conduct recurring on-site visits).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 4 of 2023 (the Egyptian Companies Law), as amended, specifically the Chapter on Limited Liability Companies governing formation, quota capital, managers, and dissolution, read together with its Executive Regulations; supplemented by the Commercial Code (Law No. 17 of 1999) on Commercial Registry requirements and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 on investor facilitation and guarantees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Incorporation and Commercial Registry Sector, operating through the unified one-stop-shop and the electronic investor services portal, Ministry of Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Foundation Contract and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Ta'sis wa Al-Nitham Al-Asasi) together with the Company Incorporation Application, filed electronically through the GAFI incorporation window, followed by automatic entry in the Commercial Registry and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for Limited Liability Company incorporation under Law No. 4 of 2023; founders fix the capital freely. For the shipyard industrial license, however, the competent authority requires the LLC to demonstrate paid-up capital commensurate with the facility's construction capacity, and the subscribed capital must be deposited in an escrow/company bank account at a bank licensed in Egypt before incorporation is completed; foreign capital contributions are certified through the Central Bank of Egypt inward-transfer procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the subscription to the founding quota capital of the Company be ratified and allocated to the founders as per the appended Subscription Schedule, and that receipt of the deposited contributions be acknowledged against the escrow bank certificate; (2) That the registered office of the Company be adopted at Plot 44, South Sector, Suez Canal Economic Zone, El-Tor, Egypt, and the Company Secretary file the registered-office particulars with the Commercial Registry; (3) That [Name A] be appointed Chief Executive Manager, [Name B] Finance Manager, and [Name C] Company Secretary, each with statutory signature authority; and (4) That the CEO complete bank account activation, GAFI registration, tax and social-insurance formalities, and initiate the shipyard licensing application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Legal-Form Selection and Pre-Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop — electronic incorporation and investor services portal (Egypt Invest digital platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online pre-reservation application for the proposed corporate name in Arabic (controlling language) with a Latin/brand variant; select Limited Liability Company as the legal form; complete the administrative pre-screening questionnaire declaring the project as construction of deep-sea dry cargo and ocean container vessels in a shipyard; authenticate the submission with the founder's digital or notarized electronic signature.
required_dossiers: Passport copies or national ID cards of all founding shareholders
Completed name-reservation and legal-form application form
Power of attorney (notarized and legalized/apostilled) if filed by an agent
Sanctions and prohibited-transactions screening declaration
Proposed trademark or corporate logo registration evidence, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or legal objection, resubmit using the second or third alternative names within 10 working days and file a written objection with the GAFI Technical Support Committee; screening flags are cured by filing a board-level enhanced due-diligence note and updated beneficial-ownership declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing and Notarization of the Foundation Deed and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Office of the Notary, Ministry of Justice) and GAFI Legal Records Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause an Arabic-language Foundation Contract and Articles of Association to be drafted strictly in accordance with the mandatory statutory clauses of Law No. 4 of 2023, fixing the quota capital division, the maritime shipbuilding object, the rules governing managers, and the audit and dispute-resolution provisions; arrange for all founders to sign before the notary public or through GAFI's remote electronic notarization module; pay the applicable stamp duties and notarization fees.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Contract and Articles of Association (Arabic controlling, bilingual presentation)
GAFI name-reservation certificate
Complete schedule of founders with allocated quota percentages
Preliminary registered-office evidence (intended lease agreement or title deed)
Identification documents and corporate authorization instruments of founding entities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary declines certification for omission of statutory clauses, cure by adopting a supplementary memorandum ratified at a founders' meeting, re-notarizing the consolidated deed; GAFI drafting comments are incorporated by filing an amended version of the deed before final compliance sign-off.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit, Escrow Bank Account Opening and Inward-Funds Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Egypt regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) and the CBE inward-transfer certification window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow bank account in the intended corporate name and deposit the subscribed quota capital (no statutory floor); obtain the bank-issued capital-deposit certificate evidencing the fully paid contributions; for foreign shareholders, complete the CBE inward-investment documentation to secure certification of the import of capital; file the ultimate beneficial-owner register and AML/KYC source-of-funds declarations.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed and pending name-reservation certificate
Bank account opening and KYC application forms
Central Bank of Egypt inward-transfer form and remitting bank statements
Corporate ownership chart and ultimate beneficial-owner register
Shipyard project description and capital-formation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank postpones account opening on AML/KYC grounds, escalate to GAFI Investor Care and resubmit with consolidated source-of-funds evidence and the projected shipyard operational plan; CBE certification queries are resolved through an amended inward-remittance narrative submitted by the remitting foreign bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing, Commercial Registry Entry and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Central Incorporation Department and Commercial Registry Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload through the GAFI electronic one-stop-shop the notarized Foundation Deed, capital-deposit certificate, registered-office proof, and the First Board (Managers) Resolution; pay the consolidated official filing fees; GAFI validates statutory conformity and directs automatic Commercial Registry entry, issuing the Certificate of Incorporation, the Commercial Registration Certificate, and the company identification file number; download certified copies and stamped deed versions.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Contract and Articles of Association
Bank capital-deposit (escrow) certificate
Registered-office lease or ownership documentation
Minutes of the First Board (Managers) Resolution
Name-reservation certificate and founder identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a correction query or refusal, cure the specified deficiencies and re-file within 30 calendar days of the query date, with a possible extension by GAFI determination; adverse incorporation decisions may be appealed to the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee without suspending parallel preparatory licensing actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Insurance and Manpower Establishment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Taxpayer Services; National Social Insurance Authority (NISA); Ministry of Manpower — Competent Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the automatic post-incorporation integration to obtain the Tax Card and Company Identification Number from ETA and register the company for corporate income tax, VAT and withholding obligations; complete the NISA social-insurance establishment file; open the establishment file with the competent Labor Office for future shipyard personnel and submit the standard employment contract templates; receive the initial workplace file confirmation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration Certificate
ETA tax-registration forms and company data record
Notarized office lease and utility evidence
Founder and manager identification documents
Manpower establishment form and employment contract templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Inconsistency notices from ETA or NISA are cured by filing a corrective data amendment through the integrated electronic correction service; late-registration penalties are waived if the correction is made within the statutory grace period; labor-office queries are resolved by a rectification memorandum and supplementary authorizations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime-Sector Pre-Licensing and Import/Export Operator Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC); Egyptian Maritime Data Center and the competent Port Authority for the yard's berthing facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an import/export economic operator in the GOEIC data registry to clear marine steel plate, ship engines, naval equipment and consumables under the correct harmonized-system codes; notify the competent seaport authority of the shipyard's quay, slipway and launching installation; open the new-construction vessel file in the Egyptian flag/classification system when the first hull is ordered; confirm applicability of strategic-zone tax incentives.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate and Tax Card
GOEIC economic-operator registration application form
Pro-forma invoices and HS-code classifications for planned marine inputs
Site plans and coordinates of the shipyard quay, dry dock and slipways
Corporate trade-workflow authorization and incoterms policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: GOEIC data-registration rejections on HS-code or provenance grounds are cured by filing an amended registration with harmonized-code justification and, where necessary, an appeal memorandum to the GOEIC Foreign-Trade Review Unit; maritime data discrepancies are resolved by amending the yard's technical description with an accredited marine-engineering statement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, operating through the 'Investia' electronic industrial licensing platform; where the shipyard is located within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone), the SCZone Industrial Licensing Center issues the same permit under identical technical standards.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License for the Shipbuilding and Ship-Repair Plant (Industrial Facility Operation License) issued under Law No. 15 of 2017 on Industrial Licensing, classified as an integrated Category (C) high-risk shipyard covering the construction of ocean-going container and dry-cargo vessels, together with the SCZone operating certificate where applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (C) high-risk project — a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report is mandatory before construction and again before commissioning, prepared by an EEAA-endorsed consultant and covering the coastal/marine baseline, acoustic and vibration modeling, ballast and dry-dock wastewater impacts, air-dispersion modeling for coating and blasting emissions, hazardous-waste logistics, and an oil-spill and emergency pollution preparedness plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All industrial wastewater and dry-dock discharges must comply with EEAA Decree No. 44 of 2000 effluent standards, including pH 6.0–9.5, TSS ≤ 60 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L; air emissions from painting, abrasive blasting and welding must meet Law No. 202 of 2020 ambient and source limits, with PM10 ≤ 50 µg/m³, PM2.5 ≤ 25 µg/m³, and VOC controls through best-available control technology and fume-extraction systems; hazardous wastes, including spent abrasives contaminated with anti-fouling paint residues, paint sludge and oily wastes, must be segregated, labeled, stored and dispatched under the EEAA manifest tracking system to a licensed hazardous-waste disposal facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority (Ministry of Interior) fire-safety certification covering a fire main ring around dry docks and quays, certified extinguishing systems for paint, thinner and flammable-liquid stores, welding-bay fire controls, and an approved emergency evacuation plan for the high-risk industrial site; structural load-inspection certificates for gantry cranes, slipways and quay walls issued by a licensed engineering consultant under Law No. 106 of 1976 and recorded with the municipal or SCZone building-control authority; Ministry of Manpower occupational-safety clearance confirming medical-examination protocols, PPE programs, confined-space entry procedures, hazardous-material storage compliance, and an active establishment file before shipyard labor forces are mobilized.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official e-portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg; e-filing portal: https://etax.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC obtains the Unified Tax Identification Number (TIN/VAT ID) by: (1) incorporating under Law No. 159 of 1981 and completing Commercial Registry registration; (2) submitting to the ETA the Tax Card application (Form 8) with notarised Articles of Association, Commercial Registry extract, tenancy/lease proof of the shipyard premises, manager/shareholder passports, and board resolution appointing the tax representative; (3) receiving the Tax Card (TIN) and mandatory VAT certificate; and (4) completing e-migration of the tax file on the ETA portal within the statutory registration period (30 days from commercial registration or from exceeding the VAT threshold). A foreign corporate shareholder may obtain a separate TIN for its Egyptian branch only if a permanent establishment arises; otherwise the Egyptian LLC registers in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Egyptian LLC is a resident corporate taxpayer separate from its shareholders, subject to Corporate Income Tax (CIT) at 22.5% under Law No. 91 of 2005; capital gains and dividends from resident Egyptian companies are generally exempt for taxed corporate shareholders; manufacturing activities located in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) or public/private free zones may elect taxation on a territorial basis with an exemption or a gross-revenue tax regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box mechanism exists. Statutory elections available: (a) Free-Zone Project election under Law 91/2005 – tax at 1% of gross FOB revenue for goods or 5% of gross revenue for services instead of standard CIT; (b) SCZONE special regime under Law 83/2002 – election of 0% CIT for up to 5 years (extendable), 0% VAT on project inputs and special customs treatment, subject to SCZONE project licence and ETA approval; (c) election to exempt dividends received from other resident taxpaying companies; and (d) standard versus actual-margin stamp duty methods. Hybrid mismatch elections are not provided under Egyptian law; income tax conventions govern tie-breaker allocation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended (effective 8 September 2016) and its Executive Regulations; administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover (goods and services); VAT registration is mandatory within 30 days of exceeding the threshold. Voluntary registration is permitted and is standard practice for shipyard exporters to claim zero-rating and refunds; no minimum capital requirement for the LLC is imposed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA e-invoicing for all registered taxpayers: invoices must be issued in ETA-prescribed XML/JSON format via ETA-certified API, ERP, or the e-invoice portal; the ETA performs near-real-time fiscal validation by assigning a unique UUID (fiscal stamp) and QR code to each invoice; e-receipts are mandatory for B2C and phased for B2B transactions; shipyards must integrate the e-invoicing API with the production ERP and issue the 0%-rate export e-invoice before goods leave the customs territory; paper invoices do not substantiate zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods and services under Article 14 of Law 67/2016, including the sale of newly-built ocean-going container vessels and offshore shipbuilding/repair services supplied to a non-resident buyer. Substantive conditions: (1) valid VAT registration; (2) actual physical export of the vessel/materials and exit from Egyptian customs territory within the statutory period; (3) consideration received in freely convertible foreign currency remitted into Egypt through a CBE-accredited bank; (4) title and risk pass to a non-resident recipient; (5) the transaction is evidenced by an ETA-validated 0%-rate e-invoice; and (6) supporting contract, delivery certificate, and foreign-currency receipt are retained for audit. Shipyard projects in SCZONE may benefit from an exemption rather than zero-rating under the SCZONE law.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ECDL release certificate / export GCC statement)
Bill of Lading (or provisional delivery certificate for vessels under construction)
Inward Remittance Certificate of foreign-currency proceeds issued by a CBE-accredited bank
Notarised Sale Contract / Shipbuilding Agreement (with title, delivery, and instalment terms)
ETA-validated electronic export invoice reflecting 0% VAT
Packing List and Certificate of Origin
Maritime vessel registration certificate / handover certificate evidencing transfer to the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA performs risk-based refund audits with a statutory 45-business-day refund issuance window; where the 0% claim is not substantiated by the full documentation bundle or the foreign-currency proceeds are not repatriated within the mandatory 180-day window (with the vessel instalment schedule subject to CBE-approved escrow/LC terms), the ETA retroactively assesses 14% VAT on the transaction plus default interest on late payment and may claw back any refund already paid. Deliberate false zero-rating exposes the LLC and its managers to criminal liability under Law 67/2016: imprisonment up to 5 years, a fine of up to 100% of the evaded VAT, an additional penalty tax of up to double the evaded amount, joint and several liability of directors and tax representatives, and closure of the shipyard for repeated violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Banking Supervision Sector and Foreign Exchange Control Department, acting under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, in coordination with the Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (AMLU) and the Egyptian Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined exchange rate system after the March 2024 floatation. Current-account transactions, including trade in goods, marine freight, port services, maritime insurance, and ordinary operating payments, are freely convertible through CBE-authorized banks. Capital-account transactions, notably direct foreign equity injection, intercompany loans, and foreign debt service, remain subject to CBE prior authorization, registration, and proper purpose-code filing. Profit and dividend remittances are permissible without a statutory cap, provided the LLC presents audited financial statements, an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax clearance certificate, and satisfies bank-level AML verification. For a shipyard registered within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone), repatriation of profits and foreign-currency proceeds may be accelerated by SCZone-specific regulations where the entity has secured the applicable SCZone incentives, but the legal entity in this pipeline is a domestic EG_LLC not explicitly identified as an SCZone invoice-issuing entity and therefore must rely on the general CBE framework. The Egyptian Pound is freely convertible for current account purposes but remains subject to liquidity management and bank matching requirements; onshore USD scarcity can delay wire execution unless the remitting bank holds strong correspondent limits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from ocean-going container vessel construction and ship repair are statutory export receipts and must be repatriated into an Egypt-resident foreign-currency account within 90 days from the date of bill of lading, vessel delivery, or official completion certificate, unless the CBE grants an extended period. The CBE's administrative directives, as amended through 2024, require banks to convert up to 50% of repatriated export proceeds into Egyptian Pounds at the prevailing declared exchange rate, while the remainder may be held in foreign currency for lawful operating use or re-export obligations. The applicable conversion ratio is set by CBE circular and is dynamic; therefore the treasury blueprint must include a currency routing matrix that captures the circular in force at the date of each receipt. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window subjects the LLC to banking penalties, denial of future trade facilities, and potential anti-money laundering escalation. The shipyard must maintain a bank-approved Export Proceeds Repatriation Schedule supported by customs export declarations, vessel delivery protocols, and matching LC drawdown records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account in EGP and USD
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account in EGP and USD
Operational Account and Maritime Installment Escrow Sub-Account
Escrow Account and Trade Finance Account in EGP and USD
Cross-Border Operational Account, Transaction Banking and Escrow Sweeping

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW and legally constrained. Egypt does not maintain an electronic money institution (EMI) passport or open-banking clearing license equivalent to the EU/UK EMI regime. Any digital wallet or e-money operation must be separately licensed by the CBE under Law No. 194 of 2020 and the CBE electronic money regulations; foreign offshore EMIs such as UK FCA-regulated or EU-licensed firms cannot open EGP-denominated corporate settlement accounts, issue escrow capacity, or provide domestic clearing rails for an Egyptian LLC without a locally licensed subsidiary or joint venture with a CBE-authorized bank. For an EG_LLC carrying a Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, reliance on an unlicensed offshore EMI would constitute a banking law violation and a critical AML red flag. The recommended compliant substitute is the transaction-banking and host-to-host portal of a top-tier Egyptian bank, optionally layered with Swift GPI for cross-border tracking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBE due-diligence rules for corporate account opening require physical presence of at least two authorized signatories and, in practice, the ultimate beneficial owner or statutory director for a mandatory in-branch interview before account activation. Fully remote digital onboarding is unavailable for a medium-risk enhanced commercial shipyard; the business scope and defense-adjacent risk of shipbuilding trigger an enhanced due diligence interview. If the LLC's director is non-resident, the bank may accept a notarized and legalized Board Resolution appointing a resident signatory with limited power of attorney, but the statutory director or UBO must still appear physically at a CBE-licensed branch for the initial risk interview. Some banks, notably NBE and CIB, may allow a hybrid route: an in-country certified true copy of the director's KYC passport, apostilled company documents, and a live video confirmation, followed by a later physical signature mission; however, this is discretionary and should not be planned as the base case. The blueprint should schedule a two-day opening mission in Cairo or Alexandria with all wet-ink original documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shipbuilding activity adjacent to naval, defense, or dual-use work which raises FATF arms-trade, proliferation-financing, and export-control red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed shipyard certificate issued by the Egyptian Authority for Maritime Safety (EAMS) and the Ministry of Transport; explicit certification that the yard constructs only commercial ISIC 3011 deep-sea container and dry cargo vessels; ISPS Code compliance statement; company policy resolution prohibiting naval and defense contracts; commercial shipbuilding contracts and technical specifications; CR extract showing primary activity as Merchant Shipbuilding; and Egyptian Customs advanced ruling confirming civilian end-use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital contribution or large installment payments received under the Maritime_Installment_LC and escrow structure from a non-resident ship-owner or charterer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-verified capital introduction file comprising notarized capital increase resolution, GAFI or SCZone registration certificate, auditor-certified source-of-funds statement for each shareholder, audited financial statements of the remitting ship-owner, underlying newbuild contract with payment milestone schedule, and per-wire reconciliation showing matching to the LC drawdown and escrow credit note.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity created by a multi-tier offshore holding structure above the Egyptian LLC, especially if any UBO resides in a sanctions-affected jurisdiction or low-credibility tax haven.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete CBE-compliant beneficial ownership chart signed by legal counsel; commercial registry filings for each intermediate entity; passport and proof of residential address for all natural-person UBOs; economic substance evidence including Egyptian payroll, shipyard lease, equipment ownership, and steel procurement contracts; negative media check and OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening reports; and sworn Board Resolution clarifying the exact source of wealth and confirming absence of politically exposed persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire flows arriving from third-party escrow agents, factoring houses, or intermediary payers rather than the direct contracted buyer, creating ambiguity on the true ordering party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed multi-party escrow or stake-holding agreement naming the Egyptian LLC as sole beneficiary; documentary evidence of the escrow provider's banking license in its home jurisdiction; full beneficial ownership structure of the escrow agent; SWIFT MT103 field 50K and field 72 remittance advice matched line-by-line to the commercial invoice; and an Egyptian counsel legal opinion confirming that the escrow mechanism does not hide the underlying principal or violate CBE exchange-control provisions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All shareholder capital injections and non-resident installment payments must arrive through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to a CBE-authorized bank account of the EG_LLC. The remittance must carry a compliant purpose description, specifically 'Direct Investment - Equity Contribution to EG LLC' or 'Capital Increase under Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2021', and must be pre-notified to the receiving bank's compliance desk. The CBE reporting system requires the receiving authorized dealer to file the inward remittance with the exchange-control code for direct investment; the LLC must simultaneously file with GAFI if the investor is in the free-zone or outside the SCZone, and must maintain an updated Egyptian CR and tax card. For capital above the bank's internal threshold, the bank will request a Board Resolution authorizing the capital capture, a legalized incorporation certificate, and appointment of the compliance contact before releasing the funds to the operational escrow. Escrow release to the operating account is permitted only after the bank has matched the wire to the capital increase resolution and the GAFI filing, and after all AML source-of-funds questions have been answered to the bank's satisfaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for trade disbursements are SWIFT MT103 for high-certainty supplier wires and irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit for major marine equipment, steel plate purchases, and sub-block construction contracts. The shipyard will issue a Maritime_Installment_LC series to upstream suppliers with payment against presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and an Egyptian-approved inspection certificate; installment disbursements under the related escrow account will be released on milestone certification by the shipyard's own naval architect and the buyer's surveyor. For operational dispatches, an Egypt-resident bank will require the LLC to submit the CBE import-form evidence or, where exempt, the matching purchase order; payments for foreign freight, insurance, and marine classification societies qualify as current-account transactions and are automatically permissible. Payments for foreign parent intercompany charges, technical royalties, or overseas debt service are capital-account events requiring CBE approval and a hard-coded underlying agreement, and must be separated from the trade flows. All outbound disbursements from the escrow ledger must be accompanied by delivery protocol certificates, builder's certificates, and a signed acceptance notice to satisfy the beneficiary bank's audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP forward contracts with CBE-authorized banks, executed with a term aligned to the shipyard's construction and installment collection cycle.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) for long-term balance-sheet hedging of capital expenditure, LC payables, and foreign-currency revenue streams, subject to CBE treasury authorization and an underlying commercial exposure.
Structured forward conversion programmes on export proceeds, allowing the LLC to fix the EGP conversion for the mandatory converted portion of export receipts.

NDF (non-deliverable forward) instruments: not permissible for direct in-country corporate hedging; an Egyptian LLC must hedge exclusively through deliverable forwards booked at a CBE-authorized onshore bank, reflecting the unified-float policy and exchange-control prohibition on offshore synthetic hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting minutes and resolutions, including approval of annual audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Commercial Registry / GAFI One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held no later than 30 June of each calendar year; corporate secretarial deposit must occur within 10 days after the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit fine of EGP 500 per day up to EGP 50,000; persistent non-compliance exposes the LLC to administrative strike-off and disqualification of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with audited annual financial statements and supporting tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due by 30 April (within four months of the 31 December fiscal-year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of 5% per month on the unpaid tax amount, capped at 10%; late-filing fine of EGP 50,000; continued default may trigger forced collection, bank account garnishment, and customs/court enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements deposited with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 July for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit accounts blocks registration of share transfers, exposes directors to civil liability, and constitutes grounds for judicial strike-off or forced liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial license renewal certificate and municipal operating fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Municipality through the GAFI One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 30 June, tied to the fiscal-year commercial license cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License suspension, daily fine of EGP 100 after the due date, and forced closure of the shipyard premises after 90 days of non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register annual confirmation and change notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Terrorism Financing Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May each year, plus a 30-day update filing after any transfer of shares or voting rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 100,000 per unregistered beneficial owner; an unregistered share transfer is not opposable to third parties and may invalidate corporate voting rights for a shipyard tendering process.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None — statutory audit is mandatory for every Egyptian LLC without size or turnover exemption. The audit must be performed by a certified accounting firm registered with the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the shipyard's audit must cover fixed-asset construction contracts, accruals, inventory, and deferred revenue in accordance with Egyptian Accounting Standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance; EAS are substantially converged with IFRS. IFRS audited statements may be prepared for consolidated group or maritime lender purposes, but the statutory filing books must remain in EAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every share transfer must first be entered in the Register of Members; any transfer resulting in direct or indirect ownership above 25% requires a GAFI beneficial-ownership update within 30 days. An annual declaration must be filed by 31 May confirming the list of natural persons who own or control the shipyard LLC, including all related corporate chains and nominee relationships.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $600 – $2,800 for registered agent and local corporate secretarial services in Cairo or Alexandria; Suez Canal Economic Zone providers can charge a higher compliance premium
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000 – $10,000 for a shipyard LLC with full work-in-progress schedules, subcontractor expenditures, and vessel-sale deferred revenue arrangements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free-zone projects may enjoy a 0% corporate income tax rate subject to payment of an annual fee of 1% of the customs value of goods imported to or exported from the free zone. Non-free-zone industrial projects may benefit from a 50% deduction of eligible capital expenditures under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and certain reduced rates for small and medium enterprises under Law No. 152 of 2020.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 41 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) electronic filing portal at erf.eta.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory quarterly advance payments during the tax year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months from the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year company, the deadline is 30 April of the following year. For a company using a 30 June fiscal year-end, the deadline is 31 October.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, tax card number, and commercial registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident permanent establishment must quote the Egyptian taxpayer identification number issued by ETA and the name of the Egyptian branch or PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Precise fiscal year-end date as adopted by the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same year-end as the PE's head office if not otherwise approved by ETA, and attach the head office declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before tax derived from all Egyptian-source activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits attributable to the Egyptian PE and connected to Egyptian-source income, as per Article 6 and DTA sourcing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation adjustments to arrive at taxable income, including disallowed expenses and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back excessive payments to foreign affiliates if not arm's length; subtract treaty-exempt dividends or free-zone income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses utilized in the year (up to 5 years of carry-forward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses of the Egyptian PE may be carried forward; home office losses are not deductible.
If treaty protections apply, the treaty rate of taxation is applied to this figure after allocating profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax at 22.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the relevant DTA rate if a claim for treaty relief has been submitted and approved; otherwise apply the 22.5% statutory rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax paid and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE may credit Egyptian quarterly advance payments, and may claim a foreign tax credit for taxes withheld on cross-border interest or royalties if a DTA provides such relief.
Any remaining tax due must be paid within 30 days of filing; otherwise monthly late-payment penalties apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EGP 5,000 plus a monthly late-payment penalty of 2% of the unpaid tax due for each month or part thereof. If no return is filed, the ETA may assess tax ex officio with an additional penalty of up to 100% of the assessed tax, and criminal proceedings may be instituted under Articles 133 and 135 of Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax for non-resident shareholders receiving dividends from a resident Egyptian company, unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit a written application to the Egyptian Tax Authority using the relevant model treaty certificate and provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), proof of beneficial ownership, and a power of attorney if represented. The ETA recommends the application be filed before the dividend distribution or at the time the withholding is reported, using the electronic claiming system. Approved treaty rates are applied retroactively, and excess tax withheld is refundable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for the use of industrial, commercial, or literary property are subject to a statutory withholding tax of 20%. Interest paid to non-resident lenders is generally subject to 20% withholding, but is reduced to 10% under several Egypt DTAs, and to 0% in certain cases for approved foreign-funded project loans. Royalty WHT rates are typically reduced under treaties to 10-15%, and interest to 10% or 0% depending on the treaty provisions and the creditor's status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be filed when related-party transactions exceed EGP 8 million in aggregate during the tax year. A Master File is mandatory when such transactions exceed EGP 40 million. Country-by-country reporting (CbCR) is required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EGP 3 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in some GCC states, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Article 109 of Law No. 91 of 2005 empowers the ETA to disregard transactions, structures, or arrangements lacking economic substance and whose sole purpose is tax avoidance. For DTA relief, the equitable approach of treaty entitlement also presupposes substantive economic activity, ownership, and substance in the residence state; asset-heavy shipbuilding operations are expected to maintain physical premises, personnel, and decision-making presence in Egypt to support treaty claims and avoid treaty abuse.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file tax returns, understatement of Egyptian-source income, manipulation of shipyard construction costs, or false invoicing of imported vessel components to inflate deductions and reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 200,000 and imprisonment for a term of 3 to 5 years under Law No. 91 of 2005, in addition to payment of the evaded tax plus a penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax and monthly late-payment interest. Repeat offenses can lead to license revocation and forced closure of the shipyard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who participate in tax evasion are personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties if the company enters insolvency or when the separate legal personality is used to commit fraud. Travel bans and seizure of personal assets may be imposed by the tax authorities or court order, and a criminal conviction results in imprisonment of the responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Arrangement / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registration of an Egyptian LLC lacking genuine premises, personnel, or shipbuilding activity, operated solely to channel dividends, interest, or royalties out of Egypt through a favorable treaty jurisdiction, or to claim CIT free-zone exemptions without real industrial operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will disregard the entity for tax purposes under Article 109 GAAR, deny treaty benefits, and reassess tax at 22.5% on all Egyptian-source income. Additional penalties of up to 100% of the tax evaded may apply, and the entity may be struck off the commercial register. In flagrant cases, prosecution for tax evasion and fraudulent commercial registration can lead to fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign declaration forms misrepresenting substance or who intentionally use a shell structure may be jointly and severally liable for all resulting corporate tax, interest, and penalties. Criminal liability for fraud can result in imprisonment, while exit bans and seizure of personal property are authorized pending payment of assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the shipyard's high-value maritime invoices, installment letters of credit, or escrow arrangements to obscure the proceeds of sanctioned arms dealing, smuggling, or fraudulent ship-purchase schemes; high-risk transactions with designated persons or jurisdictions without adequate due diligence and reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended), a corporate entity may incur fines up to EGP 1,000,000 and forfeiture of assets; senior officers face up to 10 years imprisonment. Non-compliance with beneficial ownership reporting and transaction monitoring rules results in additional CBE/Financial Regulatory Authority fines and revocation of the maritime industrial license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners can be personally prosecuted for failure to file suspicious transaction reports, knowingly facilitating money laundering, or allowing the company to be used as a conduit for proceeds. Personal liability includes imprisonment, financial fines, confiscation of personal assets, and travel restrictions under prosecutor-approved travel bans.
